deviation: The draft has no requirement to execute a DPA before processing, and replaces "documented instructions" with processing per the Customer's "documented use of the Services", so the Supplier is not bound by Arcadia's instructions. It also allows unrestricted subcontractors, with Supplier liability only "to the extent required by law" and subject to the cap in Section 11. It permits secondary use of derived data, and lets the Supplier delete data under its own retention practices. This fails the playbook (no fallback) and risks data protection non-compliance.
suggested_text:
6.1 The Supplier shall process Personal Data only on the Customer's documented instructions and in accordance with applicable data protection law. A Data Processing Agreement in the form provided by the Customer must be executed before any Personal Data is processed and in any event before go-live, and shall prevail over this Agreement in the event of conflict.
6.2 The Supplier shall maintain appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect Personal Data, as set out in the Data Processing Agreement.
6.3 The Supplier shall not engage any subcontractor or hosting provider to process Personal Data without the Customer's prior written authorisation, and shall remain fully liable for their acts and omissions. Liability under this Section 6 and the Data Processing Agreement is not subject to the limitations in Section 11.
6.4 The Supplier shall not use Personal Data, or data derived from it (including aggregated or de-identified data), for any purpose other than providing the Services to the Customer.
6.5 Upon termination or expiry, or on the Customer's request, the Supplier shall return all Customer Data in a commonly used format and then securely delete it, certifying deletion in writing within 30 days, unless law requires retention.
